record.final_answer:
Short answer: not with the current setup, but yes — with one specific change and a commercial prerequisite.

Why 5s doesn't work by polling
Nimbrel server SDK 4.x polls flag rules every 30 seconds by default, and the polling interval can't be set below 10 seconds (docs.nimbrel.example/sdk/updates, read 2026-04-20). So:

  default (30s interval)  → p100 propagation ~30s. 6x over target.
  tuned to the 10s floor  → p50 ~5s, p100 ~10s. Still fails a 5s
                            guarantee, and it hammers the API for
                            nothing.

There is no polling configuration that meets 5 seconds. The floor of 10s means the average is already your whole budget and the worst case is double it.

The path that does work: streaming
Push updates require stream: true in the client options — and that's available only on the Team plan or above. That's the real answer to "is it achievable": technically yes, commercially it depends on your tier. If you're below Team, the ask is an upgrade, and that's a purchasing conversation, not an engineering one.

What it would take
1. Confirm the plan tier. Everything below is moot if you're not on Team+.
2. Set stream: true on every service that reads the flag — in the client options at SDK init. Not one service, not the demo service. This is a code/config change requiring a redeploy of each one.
3. Add reconnect handling. A stream connection is a live socket per instance. You need backoff-and-resubscribe on drop, and a fallback poll for when the stream is down — and that fallback is 10s+ minimum, so decide explicitly what "stale for a while during an outage" means for that toggle.
4. Check the connection budget. One stream connection per replica, not per service. If you run 40 replicas across 8 services, that's 40 persistent connections; verify what the tier allows.
5. Measure end to end before promising the number. "Take effect" is ambiguous: from console save, or from flag store write? Some services cache flag values per request rather than per process — those are fine. Anything that reads flags at process start needs a restart or an on-change callback, and that path will not be 5 seconds no matter what the SDK does.
6. Verify the write path. If the console writes to a separate internal database rather than through Nimbrel's API, no SDK setting will pick it up in 5s, because the flag store never sees the change. This is the one failure mode that looks like a propagation problem but isn't.

What I'd want to know to make this concrete
Which services read the flag and whether they read per-request or cache at startup; your Nimbrel plan tier; and whether the console writes through Nimbrel's API or to its own store. With those three I can tell you whether it's a one-line option change or a redesign — and give Product a defensible estimate rather than an optimistic one.

Worth pushing back on Product about one thing: 5 seconds is a product promise that only holds while the stream is healthy. Ask what the requirement actually is — if they mean "fast enough that flipping it back during an incident is bearable," streaming clears it easily. If they mean "guaranteed bounded by 5s, always," then you're committing to a degraded-mode story as well, and that's a bigger piece of work than flipping a client option.
